nodes.summary: The triangular theta series $\psi(q) = \sum_{m \ge 0} q^{m(m+1)/2}$ is a unit of the ring $\mathbb{Z}[[q]]$ of formal power series with integer coefficients, since its constant coefficient is $1$.

nodes.summary: For integers $k, n \ge 1$, let $r_k(n)$ be the number of representations of $n$ as an ordered sum of $k$ squares of integers and $t_k(n)$ the number of representations of $n$ as an ordered sum of $k$ triangular numbers $m(m+1)/2$ with $m \ge 0$. Let $p$ be an odd prime and $\ell$ a prime with $p/2 < \ell < p$. Then $\ell$ divides both $r_\ell(p)$ and $t_\ell(p)$.
nodes.title: A prime between $p/2$ and $p$ divides the representation counts of $p$

Let $n \ge 1$, let $p$ be an odd prime with $p - 1 \ge n + 1$, and let $s$ be an integer. If $p$ does not divide $r_{s-1}(n) + r_{s-2}(n) + \cdots + r_{s-(p-1)}(n)$, then $r_s(n) \ne 0$. Likewise,…
nodes.title: Representability criterion from a window of counts

nodes.summary: The square theta series is the formal power series $\theta(q) = \sum_{m \in \mathbb{Z}} q^{m^2}$ in $\mathbb{Z}[[q]]$: for each $n \ge 0$, its coefficient of $q^n$ is the number of integers $m$ with $m^2 = n$.
nodes.title: The square theta series

nodes.summary: For an integer $k$ and $n \ge 0$, let $r_k(n)$ be the coefficient of $q^n$ in $\theta(q)^k$, where $\theta$ is the square theta series; for $k \ge 1$ it is the number of representations of $n$ as an ordered sum of $k$ squares of integers. Let $n \ge 1$ and $k \ge 1$ be integers and let $p$ be a prime with $p \ge n + 1$. If $p$ divides $r_k(n)$, then $p$ divides $r_{k+jp}(n)$ for every integer $j$.
nodes.title: Divisibility of square representation counts by a large prime is periodic

nodes.summary: For an integer $k$ and $n \ge 0$, let $r_k(n)$ be the coefficient of $q^n$ in $\theta(q)^k$, where $\theta$ is the square theta series. For every $n \ge 0$ there is a polynomial $P(z) = \sum_i c_i z^i$ with integer coefficients such that $P(z) = n! \, r_z(n)$ for every integer $z$, and every nonzero integer $k$ with $r_k(n) = 0$ divides $c_1$ and satisfies $|k| < 2 |c_i|^{1/(n-i)}$ for some $i$ with $0 \le i < n$.
nodes.title: Integer zeros of the sums-of-squares counting polynomial

nodes.summary: For an integer $k$ and $n \ge 0$, let $r_k(n)$ be the coefficient of $q^n$ in $\theta(q)^k$, where $\theta$ is the square theta series. Then for every $n \ge 0$, $r_1(n)$ equals the coefficient of $q^n$ in $\theta(q)$.
nodes.title: The one-square counts are the coefficients of the square theta series

nodes.summary: For an integer $k$ and a natural number $n$, $r_k(n)$ is the coefficient of $q^n$ in $\theta(q)^k$, where $\theta(q) = \sum_{m \in \mathbb{Z}} q^{m^2}$. Since $\theta$ has constant coefficient $1$, it is a unit of $\mathbb{Z}[[q]]$, so $\theta^k$ is a power series for negative $k$ as well.
nodes.title: Representation numbers for sums of squares

nodes.summary: For an integer $k$, let $t_k(n)$ be the coefficient of $q^n$ in $\psi(q)^k$, where $\psi(q) = \sum_{m \ge 0} q^{m(m+1)/2}$. Let $n \ge 1$ and $k \ge 1$ be natural numbers and let $p$ be a prime with $p \ge n + 1$. If $p$ divides $t_k(n)$, then $p$ divides $t_{k+rp}(n)$ for every integer $r$.

Let $n \ge 1$ and let $p$ be an odd prime with $p - 1 \ge n + 1$. For every integer $s$, if $p$ does not divide $\sum_{i=1}^{p-1} t_{s-i}(n)$, then $t_s(n) \ne 0$.

nodes.summary: The logarithmic coefficients $b_n$ of the triangular theta series satisfy $b_1 = 1$, $b_2 = -1/2$ and $b_3 = 4/3$; this matches the expansion $\log(1 + q + q^3 + \cdots) = q - q^2/2 + 4q^3/3 + \cdots$.
nodes.title: First logarithmic coefficients of the triangular theta series

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, let $b_n$ be the rational number $b_n = \sum_{d \mid n,\ n/d \text{ odd}} 1/d - \sum_{d \mid n,\ n/d \text{ even}} 1/d$, where $d$ runs over the positive divisors of $n$; for $n = 0$ the sums are taken to be empty, so $b_0 = 0$.
nodes.title: Logarithmic coefficients of the triangular theta series

nodes.summary: The triangular theta series is the formal power series $\psi(q) = \sum_{m \ge 0} q^{m(m+1)/2}$ with integer coefficients: for each natural number $n$, its coefficient of $q^n$ is the number of natural numbers $m$ with $m(m+1)/2 = n$.
